rule.title: Contract with external calls and state mutations lacks a reentrancy guard slot

intent.attack_thesis: A contract makes external calls and mutates state but has no reentrancy guard storage slot, leaving all external-call-bearing functions vulnerable to re-entry attacks.

reporting.title_template: Contract lacks reentrancy guard despite external calls and state mutations
reporting.summary: Matches contracts that contain external calls and state-mutating operations but have no storage slot functioning as a reentrancy mutex.
reporting.user_summary: This contract makes external calls and changes its own state but does not implement a reentrancy guard. Without a mutex lock, any function that sends ETH or calls another contract can be re-entered before its state updates complete, potentially allowing an attacker to drain funds.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector scans the contract-level state model for the presence of EXTERNAL_CALL_OBSERVED alongside asset_transfer effects. It then checks whether any storage slot is tagged as a reentrancy guard. Absence of such a slot indicates the contract relies on no programmatic reentrancy protection, making all functions with external calls susceptible to classic reentrancy.
reporting.exploit_narrative: An attacker identifies a function that transfers ETH or tokens via an external call and updates balances afterward. Because there is no reentrancy mutex, the attacker's receive/fallback function re-enters the same or a different function, exploiting the pre-update state to withdraw repeatedly until the contract is drained.
exploit_preconditions: the contract makes external calls (CALL opcode) that trigger code execution in untrusted contracts
the contract mutates state that controls asset transfers
no storage slot acts as a reentrancy guard (nonReentrant, mutex, or equivalent)
remediation_hints: implement a reentrancy guard using OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard or equivalent mutex pattern
ensure all functions with external calls use the nonReentrant modifier
adopt the checks-effects-interactions pattern across all state-mutating functions

preconditions: external call emitted before state finalized

steps.action: call victim function that issues external call before updating state
steps.expected_state: attacker callback re-enters victim function before state is updated

steps.action: callback re-enters and withdraws/mints again based on stale state

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker drains more value than their balance entitles them to via reentrancy
